paper.title: Deep autoregressive models for the efficient variational simulation of many-body quantum systems
paper.authors: Or Sharir, Yoav Levine, Noam Wies, Giuseppe Carleo, Amnon Shashua

results.system_description: Transverse-field Ising, 12 × 12 · h/J = 2 · open. H = -J sum_<ij> sigma^z_i sigma^z_j - h sum_i sigma^x_i; Pauli matrices; J = 1; h = 2; no constant shift
results.source_location: Table "Estimates of the ground state energies of the transverse-field Ising model" (table:ground_state_values), row Gamma = 2.0J, column "NAQS Energy"
results.eligibility_evidence: Variational energy per site of the autoregressive network, estimated from exact (i.i.d.) samples; the QMC and PEPS columns are other calculations.
results.notes: H = -J sum sigma^z_i sigma^z_j - Gamma sum sigma^x_i with Pauli matrices, 12 x 12 lattice with open boundaries (Experiments); energy per site. Full Hilbert space, sampled autoregressively.

results.system_description: Heisenberg, 10 × 10 · J = 1 · open · Sz = 0. H = J sum_<ij> S_i · S_j; spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2; J = 1; no constant shift
results.source_location: Table "Ground state energies for the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model with open boundary conditions" (table:heisenberg), row 10 x 10, column NAQS
results.eligibility_evidence: Variational energy per site of the autoregressive network, estimated from exact (i.i.d.) samples; the QMC and PEPS columns are other calculations.
results.notes: The paper writes H = sum sigma_i · sigma_j with Pauli matrices, but the printed energies are per site in the S = sigma/2 convention of the instance: the QMC energies of the same table (-0.628656(2), -0.643531(2), Liu et al.) are the S = 1/2 values, so no convention factor is applied. Open boundaries; full Hilbert space sampled autoregressively (the ground state is the Sz = 0 singlet).
